name: DeviceOrientation and DeviceMotion events
plain: Tilt and shake data from the phone; iOS asks first, Android Chrome does not.
meaning: Reveals how the device is held and moved: tilt, walking cadence, vehicle vibration. Research has inferred PINs and keystrokes from tilt patterns, and it hints at device class.

access.prompt_ui: iOS Safari 13+: system alert asking for Motion and Orientation access, Allow or Don't Allow, after requestPermission(). Chrome and Firefox on Android: no prompt, Motion sensors site setting defaults to Allow. Most desktops: events do not fire.
access.persistence: iOS: remembered for the page session and re-asked after the page process ends; Chrome: site setting Allow or Block per origin
access.revocation: iOS: Settings > Safari > Advanced > Motion & Orientation Access (iOS 12.2 global switch); Chrome: Site settings > Motion sensors
access.iframe: Cross-origin iframes blocked unless allow="accelerometer; gyroscope; magnetometer" (Chrome 76+)
steps: iOS: call requestPermission() inside a click handler
Add listeners; events fire at about 60 Hz while the tab is visible

chrome.note: Secure context required from 50; no prompt

safari.note: iOS 13 added requestPermission; macOS Safari has no motion sensors

fields.name: alpha
fields.precision: about 0.1 degree; absolute only on deviceorientationabsolute

limits.headline: Can sense how your phone is tilted and shaken, sometimes only after you allow it
limits.user_action: You open a tilt based page, like a game or AR view, and tap Allow on iPhone
can: Measure tilt, turning and shaking while the page is open
Spot walking steps or vehicle bumps
Move a view or game as you tilt the phone
cannot: Run without your Allow on iPhone Safari 13 and later
Measure motion while the page is closed or in the background
Be blocked by default on Android Chrome and Firefox; they allow it unless you turn Motion sensors off
Know your location; it only senses motion
limits.differs: iPhone Safari asks first. Chrome and Firefox on Android allow it unless you block Motion sensors in site settings.

story.what_it_is: The page feels how you tilt and shake your phone.

marketing.name: Device orientation events
marketing.pitch: Describes events that tell pages how a device is tilted and moved, used for compasses, games and 360 views.

story.for_you: You tilt your phone and a 360 photo turns, a marble rolls or a compass needle moves. On iPhone a prompt asks first. On many Android browsers there is no prompt at all.
story.for_makers: Tilt makes web games, AR and photo viewers feel alive without an app. It is also read by trackers, since small sensor quirks are a fingerprint, and research has shown typing can be guessed from motion.

use_cases.example: A browser racing or balance game lets you steer by tilting your phone.
A web AR try on or furniture placement page uses tilt to place a sofa in your room.
A web map or compass turns the arrow as you turn your phone.
A 360 degree video or virtual tour pans as you move your phone.
A web workout counter uses shakes and steps to count reps or steps.
Researchers showed that a page can infer typed PINs from tilt, which is why iPhone asks first.
A fraud tool checks for believable motion, because a phone farm or emulator has none.

technical_bounds: iOS requires a user gesture to request
No events when the tab is hidden

abuse: PIN and keystroke inference from motion (published attacks)

history.change: Orientation and motion events restricted to secure contexts
Motion and Orientation access disabled by default behind a setting
requestPermission() added; per-site prompt replaces the global setting
Cross-origin iframes need accelerometer, gyroscope, magnetometer policy
